To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the N-terminal eLRR-flanking region of Cf-9 is essential for activity and that the 22 N-glycosylation sites contribute to activity by providing a glycan shield for the recognition surface and by stabilizing the protein.

the N-terminal LRF domain of Cf-9 is important for activity, that the N-glycosylation of Cf-9 contributes to its activity, and that the N-terminal eLRF domain and N-glycosites of Cf-9 are conserved in many eLRR proteins.

Cf-9 is an eLRR receptor-like protein with 22 N-glycosylation sites and that recognition specificity and protein stability are determined by the N-terminal eLRR-flanking domain and the LRR modules, respectively, and that the LRR modules and N-terminal domain are connected by a linker that is essential for protein stability.
In summary, our research is concerned with

structure–function analysis in a large class of proteins, and it shows that a combination of mutagenesis and modeling of the protein structure is a powerful approach for the analysis of the structure and function of eLRR proteins.
the structure and function of Cf-9 and other eLRRs.
a large class of proteins with eLRRs that play key roles in the recognition of pathogens and hormones in plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N-terminal LRF and the C-terminal LRRs are both essential for activity and that the N-terminal domain is involved in recognition specificity.
eLRR proteins are stabilized by glycosylation and that recognition of pathogen effectors is achieved by specific contacts between the concave β-sheet surfaces of the eLRR domains and the effectors.

the Cf-9 eLRR protein, and possibly other eLRRs, is a receptor-like protein with a concave surface for specific recognition and with a convex surface for interaction with other proteins, including the cognate elicitor and the Avr9 effector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cf-9 activity depends critically on its overall structure, which is stabilized by N-glycanylation and by Trp/Cys pairs, and that specific recognition depends on a concave surface of the protein.

the eLRR proteins are modular proteins with a conserved architecture, in which the LRRs are important for protein stability and probably function as a platform for recognition, while the N-terminal domain is essential for recognition and may be important for protein stability as well.
Cf-9 is a highly structured protein with an N-terminal domain that has a role in recognition and a large eLRR domain that is essential for protein stability.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the structure–function analysis presented here can be used to predict the function of eLRRs in other species, and that the results of such analyses may help to guide the rational design of novel disease-resistant crops.
the structure of eLRR proteins can be predicted from the sequence, and the structure is a good guide to the function of these proteins.
the structure of Cf-9 is highly constrained and that the LRRs are not just a simple repeating unit.
